chapters.title: Visions of God
chapters.summary: Among the exiles by the river Chebar, Ezekiel sees a storm of fire with four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, and above them the glory of the Lord on a throne.

chapters.title: Ezekiel's call
chapters.summary: God sends Ezekiel to rebellious Israel: whether they hear or refuse, they will know a prophet has been among them. He is given a scroll of lament.

chapters.title: The watchman
chapters.summary: Ezekiel eats the scroll and it tastes like honey. God makes him a watchman for Israel, responsible to warn the wicked.

chapters.title: The siege acted out
chapters.summary: Ezekiel acts out the siege of Jerusalem with a clay tablet, lying on his side for many days and eating rationed bread.

chapters.title: The shaved hair
chapters.summary: Ezekiel shaves his head and divides the hair into thirds, showing how Jerusalem's people will die by plague, sword and scattering.

chapters.title: Against the mountains
chapters.summary: God will destroy the idolatrous shrines on Israel's mountains, but a remnant will remember Him.

chapters.title: The end has come
chapters.summary: Disaster is coming on the land. Silver and gold will not save them in the day of the Lord's wrath.

chapters.title: Idols in the temple
chapters.summary: In a vision Ezekiel is taken to Jerusalem and sees elders worshiping idols in the temple and men bowing to the sun.

chapters.title: The mark on the foreheads
chapters.summary: A man marks the foreheads of those who grieve over Jerusalem's sins, and judgment begins at the sanctuary.

chapters.title: Coals from the cherubim
chapters.summary: Burning coals from among the cherubim are scattered over the city, and the glory of the Lord rises from the temple threshold.

chapters.title: A new heart
chapters.summary: God judges the corrupt leaders, but promises the exiles: I will give them one heart and put a new spirit within them. The glory leaves the city.

chapters.title: Packing for exile
chapters.summary: Ezekiel packs his bags and digs through a wall as a sign of exile. God's word will no longer be delayed.

chapters.title: False prophets
chapters.summary: Woe to prophets who follow their own spirit and whitewash a crumbling wall, crying peace when there is none.

chapters.title: Idols in the heart
chapters.summary: Elders who set up idols in their hearts will not receive an answer. Even Noah, Daniel and Job could save only themselves.

chapters.title: The useless vine
chapters.summary: Jerusalem is like a vine branch that is good for nothing but fuel.

chapters.title: The unfaithful bride
chapters.summary: God found Jerusalem as an abandoned baby, raised her and married her, but she turned to idols. Yet He will remember His covenant and make atonement.

chapters.title: Two eagles and a cedar
chapters.summary: A parable of two eagles and a vine pictures Judah's broken treaty with Babylon. God will plant a tender cedar sprig that becomes a great tree.

chapters.title: The soul that sins
chapters.summary: Each person is responsible for their own sin. God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked: turn and live. Make yourselves a new heart.

chapters.title: Lament for the princes
chapters.summary: A funeral song for Judah's kings, pictured as young lions caught and a vine uprooted.

chapters.title: Israel's history of rebellion
chapters.summary: God recounts Israel's rebellion from Egypt onward, yet acted for His name's sake. He will gather them and accept them.

chapters.title: The sword of the Lord
chapters.summary: God's sword is sharpened against Jerusalem. The crown will be overturned until he comes whose right it is.

chapters.title: The bloody city
chapters.summary: Jerusalem's sins are listed. God looks for someone to stand in the gap, and finds none.

chapters.title: Two sisters
chapters.summary: A parable of two unfaithful sisters, Oholah and Oholibah, picturing Samaria and Jerusalem chasing foreign powers.

chapters.title: The cooking pot
chapters.summary: Jerusalem is a pot set on the fire. Ezekiel's wife dies, and he is told not to mourn openly, as a sign to the people.

chapters.title: Ammon, Moab, Edom and Philistia
chapters.summary: Judgment on neighbors who rejoiced at Jerusalem's fall, so that they will know He is the Lord.

chapters.title: Against Tyre
chapters.summary: Tyre gloated over Jerusalem, so it will become a bare rock where fishermen spread their nets.

chapters.title: Lament for Tyre
chapters.summary: Tyre is pictured as a magnificent trading ship that sinks in the heart of the seas.

chapters.title: The king of Tyre
chapters.summary: The proud king of Tyre, who said "I am a god", was perfect in beauty, in Eden, until iniquity was found in him. Sidon is also judged.

chapters.title: Against Egypt
chapters.summary: Pharaoh, the great monster of the Nile, will be humbled, and Egypt given to Nebuchadnezzar.

chapters.title: Egypt's day of doom
chapters.summary: The day of the Lord is near for Egypt and its allies, and Pharaoh's arms will be broken.

chapters.title: The fallen cedar
chapters.summary: Assyria was a magnificent cedar that fell because of its pride; Egypt will fall the same way.

chapters.title: Lament for Pharaoh
chapters.summary: Pharaoh is lamented as he goes down to the pit with the fallen nations.

chapters.title: The watchman again
chapters.summary: Ezekiel is reminded he is a watchman. As I live, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked. News arrives that Jerusalem has fallen.

chapters.title: The good shepherd
chapters.summary: God condemns Israel's shepherds who fed themselves. He Himself will seek His sheep, set over them one shepherd, His servant David, and make a covenant of peace.

chapters.title: Against Mount Seir
chapters.summary: Edom, which cherished hatred and wanted Israel's land, will be made desolate.

chapters.title: A new heart and a new spirit
chapters.summary: God will bring Israel home for His name's sake, sprinkle clean water on them, and give them a new heart and His own Spirit.

chapters.title: The valley of dry bones
chapters.summary: Ezekiel prophesies to a valley of dry bones. They come together, breath enters them, and they live, a picture of Israel's restoration. Two sticks become one.

chapters.title: Gog of Magog
chapters.summary: A future invader, Gog, comes against a restored Israel, and God shows His greatness by defeating him.

chapters.title: Gog defeated
chapters.summary: Gog's armies fall, and God will no longer hide His face from Israel, for He has poured out His Spirit on them.

chapters.title: The new temple
chapters.summary: In a vision Ezekiel is shown a new temple and a man with a measuring rod who measures its gates and courts.

chapters.title: The temple measured
chapters.summary: The sanctuary, the Most Holy Place and the side rooms of the visionary temple are measured.

chapters.title: The priests' rooms
chapters.summary: The rooms for the priests and the outer walls of the temple area are measured, separating the holy from the common.

chapters.title: The glory returns
chapters.summary: The glory of the Lord returns from the east and fills the temple. God says this is the place of His throne, where He will dwell forever.

chapters.title: The prince and the priests
chapters.summary: The east gate stays shut, for God has entered by it. Rules are given for priests who teach the difference between holy and common.

chapters.title: Land and offerings
chapters.summary: A sacred district is set apart, and rulers are told to do justice and use honest measures.

chapters.title: Worship in the new temple
chapters.summary: Instructions for the prince's offerings on Sabbaths, new moons and feasts.

chapters.title: The river from the temple
chapters.summary: Water flows from under the temple, growing into a river that brings life wherever it goes, with trees whose leaves are for healing.

chapters.title: The Lord is there
chapters.summary: The land is divided among the tribes, and the city will be named: The Lord is there.
